newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW-POLITICAL ANALYSTS COMMENTS ON UK ELECTION.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-POLITICAL ANALYSTS COMMENTS ON UK ELECTION.

text.p: Following is a selection of comments from political analysts on the outcome of Britain's May 1 parliamentary election, made as results were announced.
2245 GMT - IVOR CREWE, VICE CHANCELLOR AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ESSEX (after the first handful of results)
"The results are not suggesting a 12 percent swing which is what the exit polls are suggesting. They are suggesting more of an eight or nine percent swing," Crewe told BBC World Service Television.

"Either the exit polls are somewhat out and the swing is not as great as we think or the anti-Conservative swing is going to be much larger in other parts of the country, particularly in the south and London and in Conservative seats. If that happens, the Conservatives may well indeed lose even more seats than we've been predicting."
2220 GMT - DAVID BUTLER, LEADING BRITISH VOTING TRENDS ANALYST AND OXFORD UNIVERSITY ACADEMIC (after Hamilton South result)

"We've had four safe seats and they've all stayed with Labour. We've seen the swing, it's obviously moving, not so much in Scotland as elsewhere. The SNP were down, the Referendum Party are the one thing we've seen but a negligible vote. The Liberal Democrats (are) holding up even in seats which they haven't got a prayer of winning."
2145 GMT (after broadcasters' exit polls pointed to overwhelming Labour majority) -- "This is much the biggest thing to happen to any party since the war. It is a turnover of monumental scale."
2138 GMT --ANTHONY KING, PROFESSOR OF GOVERNMENT AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ESSEX

"(This) is like an asteroid destroying practically all life on earth. This is an extraordinary result. There's been nothing like it -- if this is what is going to happen -- since the second world war. There's been nothing like it in this century. Most notable has been the total collapse of the Conservative vote. Labour is doing very well and the Conservatives are doing horrendously badly."
2110 GMT - MICHAEL THRASHER, PROFESSOR OF POLITICS AT PLYMOUTH UNIVERSITY

"The Conservatives haven't polled this figure since 1832. So this election could be of historic proportions...The latest Gallup regional poll pointed to a majority of over 200 (seats, but) the exit figures are far more reliable. We are now looking around a Labour majority of around 160 to 180 seats."
2118 GMT - COLIN RALLINGS, PROFESSOR OF POLITICS AT PLYMOUTH UNIVERSITY (after MORI exit poll for ITN television news)

"It is in line with the campaign polls. A number of people thought it couldn't happen but if it does, Labour will have its largest majority ever, the Conservatives will have their lowest share of the vote since at least 1859, and their could be the largest third party in parliament since 1923 -- An historic night indeed."
